description:
The file `src/ocaml/lib/ai_linter/crystal_rules.ml` is 1921 lines and the largest source file in the project (~5x the next largest). It mixes six distinct concerns:

1. File path detection helpers (is_test_or_spec_file)
2. AST expression-tree walking helpers (get_name_chain, get_full_name, collect_app_names)
3. Hallucinated-method database (~80 lines of static data)
4. 30+ individual rule detectors
5. Rule registry (all ())
6. Main analysis entrypoint (analyze_module)

It also contains two confirmed bugs where duplicate top-level `let` definitions silently shadow the correct version (OCaml allows this without warning by default; the dune flags suppress warnings but not this one).

This epic tracks the refactor: split the file by concern, fix the two bugs, extract shared combinators, hoist magic numbers to a config record, and standardize error message formatting.

Public API surface is `Crystal_rules.analyze_module : CatseyeAST.t -> Types.finding list` only — safe to refactor freely.

Children:
- catseye-XXX: BUG: detect_data_clump defined twice, first is broken
- catseye-XXX: BUG: count_nodes in detect_long_method defined twice, second misses ETryCatchFinally
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: split detectors by category into submodules
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: extract shared AST walker / detector combinator (DRY)
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: move hallucinated method DB to its own module
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: hoist magic numbers into a config record
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: standardize error message format
- catseye-XXX: REFACTOR: simplify is_test_or_spec_file using Base String.contains
title: Refactor crystal_rules.ml (1921 lines) into focused modules
